<page>
 Brazoria County District Court
 Cause No. 2023-CV-0042
 Joshua Lee, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Oral Deposition of Joshua Lee
Date:
March 28, 2024
Location:
Offices of Santiago & Romero Law Group
Examining attorney:
Stephanie Williams, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defending attorney:
Eric Phillips, Santiago & Romero Law Group
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record for this part. You can use "the plaintiff."
Q: Understood. Let's start with the accident. Where did it happen?
A: On a surface street in Pasadena, Texas, in the right lane headnig toward a shopping area.
Q: What were you doing right before the collision?
A: I was driving at a normal speed and I signaled to move from the right lane into the middle lane. I checked my mirror and
glanced over my shoulder. I didn't see anything beside me.
Q: What happened next?
A: As I started to merge, I felt a hard bump on the driver's side. The other vehicle had come up alongside me and scraped along
my door. My car jerked toward the curb, and I had to correct it.
Q: Did you stop after the impact?
A: Yes, I pulled into a parking lot about a hundred feet ahead. The other driver stopped too, and we exchanged information.
Q: When did you first notice pain in your neck?
A: Not right away. About an hour later, I started to feel stiffness at the base of my skull and a dull ache running into my
shoulders. By the next morning it was harder to turn my head to check blind spots.
Q: What treatment have you received?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic the same day, and then I saw my primary care doctor. They recommended rest, over-the-counter
pain relievers, and a set of physical therapy sessions. I've been attending those sessions twice a week.
Q: How has the neck pain affected your daily life?
A: It's made simple things harder. I have trouble sleeping through the night because I can't find a comfortable position. I've cut
back on driving longer distances, and I had to stop going to my weekend tennis league for a while. Lifting groceries also causes a
sharp twinge.
Q: Have you returned to any of those activities?
A: Partly. I'm back on light household chores and I drive short trips, but I still get tired and sore by the afternoon. My physical
therapist says I'm making progress, though I'm not back to where I was before the accident.
Q: Thank you. Nothing further at this time.
</page>
